description: Creation of 6no. self-contained flats with associated cycle and bin storage, following the change of use of first floor from office (Class E) to residential (Class C3), the erection of a two storey rear extension with balconies and terraces and alterations to rear building including an additional storey and terraces. Retention and reconfiguration of the Class E unit at ground floor level with alterations to fenestration.
decision_conditions: The proposed development, by reason of its cumulative scale, bulk and visual complexity, including extensive alterations to the roof of the locally listed building and the addition of a further storey to the rear building, would result in an overdevelopment of the site. The proposal would materially alter the established proportions and roofscape, erode the legibility of the building's neo-Georgian design, and diminish the prominence of key features, resulting in a dominant and intrusive form of development that fails to preserve the character and appearance of the Ruislip Village Conservation Area and harms the significance of the locally listed building. This represents a clear departure from the form of development previously found acceptable at appeal. The identified less than substantial harm is not outweighed by the limited public benefits of the proposal and is therefore contrary to Policies BE1 and HE1 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part One (2012), Policies DMHB 1, DMHB 4 and D

The proposed development, by reason of the additional storey to the rear building and associated increase in height and bulk, would result in an overbearing form of development that would cause an unacceptable loss of outlook and sense of enclosure to neighbouring occupiers, in particular the first-floor rear bedroom window at No. 80A High Street and No.2  Ickenham Rd. The proposal would therefore result in harm to the residential amenity of adjoining occupiers, contrary to Policy DMHB 11 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part Two (2020), Policy D3 of the London Plan (2021), and the National Planning Policy Framework (2024).

The decision to REFUSE planning permission has been taken having regard to all relevant planning legislation, regulations, guidance, circulars and Council policies, including The Human Rights Act (1998) (HRA 1998) which makes it unlawful for the Council to act incompatibly with Convention rights, specifically Article 6 (right to a fair hearing); Article 8 (right to respect for private and family life); Article 1 of the First Protocol (protection of property) and Article 14 (prohibition of discrimination).

The decision to REFUSE planning permission has been taken having regard to the policies and proposals in the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 1 (2012) and Part 2 (2020) set out below, including Supplementary Planning Guidance, and to all relevant material considerations, including The London Plan (2021) and national guidance.

This is a reminder that Under the terms of the Planning Act 2008 (as amended) and Community Infrastructure Levy Regulations 2010 (as amended), should an application for appeal be allowed, the proposed development would be deemed as 'chargeable development' and therefore liable to pay the London Borough of Hillingdon Community Infrastructure Levy (CIL) and the Mayor of London's Community Infrastructure Levy (CIL). This would be calculated in accordance with the London Borough of Hillingdon CIL Charging Schedule 2014 and the Mayor of London's CIL Charging Schedule 2012.
For more information on CIL matters please visit the planning portal page at: www.planningportal.gov.uk/planning/applications/howtoapply/whattosubmit/cil
